To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Threshold points before the issue list

1. **The "[STANDARD]" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" do not bind us.** The Seller's package says [STANDARD] clauses were "cleared by both sides" and need no scrutiny. That is the counterparty's own characterisation. Every issue below has been reviewed against our playbook, and most of the [STANDARD]-labelled clauses are the most adverse to us.
2. **The claim that terms were "settled at principal level" and are "FINAL" is unverified and contradicts our playbook.** No written authority from Amelia Frost exists for any fallback (20% cap, 18 months, post-Completion Riverlark release). Unless Amelia confirms otherwise in writing, by reference to this draft, nothing is agreed.
3. **The "market context" preamble is advocacy, not evidence.** Our positions come from the playbook, not from the Seller's statement of what is "standard".
4. **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter undercuts several of its SPA positions.** Bluefen consent is not provided, Riverlark is unpaid, bonuses are excluded from the funds flow, the DD-006 scope is unknown, and DD-012 is not independent verification. These admissions support our mark-up.

---

## Issue-by-issue

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)**
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% fallback is usable only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and restore 25% / AUD 6,000,000. *The Seller has opened at our authority-gated fallback, and we have no authority to concede it.*

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket (cl 12.2)**
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess only (deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; recovery from the first dollar once exceeded (tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *These thresholds are five times ours, and a deductible structure removes the first AUD 250,000 of every proven loss.*

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3/13)**
- **Seller:** 18 months, plus a rider that any limitation applies to *all* Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims. 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **Recommendation:** Reject, restore 24 months, and delete the "all Claims" rider (see N-014). *18 months is unauthorised, and the rider silently imports the general regime into every other category.*

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties fall under the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and exclusion from the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Title and capacity are what we are paying AUD 24m for, and capping them at 20% for 18 months is not an administrative point.*

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)**
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature". There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is non-waivable.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert an express carve-out. *The "any nature" wording would purport to protect fraud, which our playbook says no one may waive.*

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7; DL 1.1–1.2)**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room as at 22 Sept 2026, the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only. No whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Delete DL 1.1–1.2 and keep specific disclosures 2–10, subject to a fair-disclosure standard. *Blanket disclosure would neutralise the warranties. The Seller's assertion that we "accepted the disclosure framework" is incorrect.*

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, or that was discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any qualifier must use named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3. *Imputed adviser knowledge plus "discoverable" is a back door to whole-data-room disclosure, and it would gut the specific indemnities.*

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only, with the consent deemed satisfied on delivery of a written consent. DL 2 admits there is no final consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent *and* evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a Completion condition. Not consent-on-delivery, and not reasonable endeavours alone.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Make it a hard condition precedent, with conditions-satisfaction evidence as a Completion deliverable. *Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (AUD 3.6m), and a delivered-but-ineffective consent leaves us exposed.*

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2/7)**
- **Seller:** The release is "to be provided following Completion". DL 3 says the facility is not repaid and no discharge exists, with about AUD 3.2m outstanding.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release requires an irrevocable lender undertaking *and* Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Require a payout letter, a funds-flow line paying Riverlark directly, and executed releases (or an irrevocable undertaking, if Amelia approves) at Completion. *Debt-free pricing means nothing if encumbered shares and assets transfer to us.*

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (funds flow; DL 5)**
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised. On-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus any triggered payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs, either as a specific funds-flow line item or as Debt or Seller-funded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the silent exclusion. Add an itemised deduction or Seller funding, plus an indemnity for on-costs. *The bonuses are triggered by Completion and fall on the Company we are buying, so if they are not itemised we pay twice.*

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and called "adequate".
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering Ironquay IP ownership and transfer, third-party claims and remediation, while preserving the SOW3 payment cure. Treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified in either direction (DL 4 itself says it is not bank-verified).
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow form. Broaden the indemnity, require proof of cleared payment or a confirmatory assignment as a deliverable, and keep the SOW3 cure. *Under DD-004 cl 7.3 the transfer of SOW3 materials depends on payment, so the exposure is IP ownership, not just a fee.*

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL 6)**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material.
- **Buyer wants:** Preservation of logs, a completed investigation, and regular updates to us before Completion. No assumption of a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller's characterisation. Add pre-Completion covenants (preserve evidence, investigate, update the Buyer, consult on any notification decision) and preserve warranty and indemnity rights. *Scope and access are unknown (about 1,240 records), so neither "immaterial" nor "breach" is established.*

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DL 8)**
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs of AUD 330,000 (3 × 110,000).
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment first, with no automatic Debt classification or price deduction either way.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept "ordinary course" as settled. Request information on whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable or accrued, and on timing across DD-008/DD-011, then classify. *The disclosure itself says this is undetermined, and our playbook prohibits pre-judging it in either direction.*

**SPA-N-014: Category separation (cl 12.3 rider; 9.3/12.8/20.5)**
- **Seller:** Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature". Tax and IP are folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment/indemnity and covenant categories kept separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Delete the default-application rider and expressly confine general limitations to general Warranty Claims. *The rider is exactly the hidden override the playbook prohibits.*

**SPA-N-015: Title verification (DL 10)**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register. DL 10 concedes this is the Seller's source and not Buyer verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, such as ASIC extracts, PPSR searches, share certificates, board and shareholder approvals, and confirmation of no options or rights. DD-012 is an internal source only.
- **Recommendation:** Reject reliance on DD-012 alone. Require independent title evidence as a Completion deliverable, backed by the uncapped Fundamental regime. *An internal register prepared by the Seller is not proof, and Riverlark security may affect the shares.*

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP terms remain OPEN. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled". Mark tax and IP as open for separate negotiation outside the general cap, basket and time limit. *Nothing has been agreed, and the Seller's label would cap tax and IP at 20% for 18 months by default.*

---

## Suggested next steps
1. Reply to Seller counsel: the [STANDARD]/FINAL labels are not accepted, no positions are agreed, and our mark-up follows.
2. **Confirm with Amelia Frost** whether any principal-level discussion took place. If she wants to authorise any fallback (20% cap, 18 months, post-Completion Riverlark release), it must be in writing and reference this draft.
3. Information requests: Bluefen consent and cl 11.3 evidence; Riverlark payout letter; bonus on-cost calculation; Ironquay payment or assignment evidence; DD-006 investigation status and logs; Sandbar renewal terms; independent title searches.
